question: Which surviving guest interfaces constrain a candidate replacement of D3D API bodies, independently of the shader patcher and command replay implementation?

scope.classification: This is a surveyed region, not a proved library extent. Per-body device/resource behavior and accepted client identities assign roles. Six known middleware clients inside it and unclassified bodies remain outside an automatic D3D classification. Outside-region utility callers are not automatically gameplay code.
scope.boundary: Static constraints and candidate policy. No exhaustive device/object alias census, ABI replacement implementation, complete callback/lifetime contract, runtime parity or safe renderer cutover.

dependencies.use: Accepted indexed draw roots; this inventory was partial.
Canonical API role evidence, outside caller/site counts, table registration, nine inline writers and partial ownership classification.
Published device identity through *(*0x820009F0), without a complete lifetime contract.
Canonical bindings, object field layouts, resource prefixes and constructor-specific surface fields.
Title-requested constant readback, retained shader output slots and subsequent rebinding.
Qualified mapped-program identity, shader construction and persistent versus allocated patch consumers.
Existing fence, event, callback and presentation wait dependencies.
Conditional replay effects and unresolved worker callback, completion and ownership boundaries.

currentEvidence.method: Serial foreground read-only no-analysis queries through tools/run-headless.ps1, maintained ghidra/DumpMemoryWords.java, ghidra/FindDirectCallers.java, ghidra/FindSplitConstantCandidates.java and ghidra/FindPointerValues.java; bounded exact-function generated corroboration. A read-only syntactic publication-load query additionally matched lis/lwz pairs without register-lifetime analysis.
currentEvidence.inputQualification: native-renderer-shader-fetch-patch-boundary.json#/currentEvidence/inputQualification applies. A fresh comparison reproduced the mapped digest, 470 differing bytes in 60 ranges confined to the historical thunk envelope. Cited semantic words avoid that envelope. Raw whole-mapped-program counts are not unmodified-image or indirect-call absence proofs.

deviceDispatchReads.label: V
deviceDispatchReads.claim: The client loads G from renderer wrapper+0xF54, reads a function pointer at G+0x40+s and calls it with G and the table-provided value. s is a byte offset. 0x82517630, 0x82519328 and 0x825193B0 provide further setter-table clients.

deviceDispatchReads.label: V
deviceDispatchReads.claim: The client loads G from renderer wrapper+0xF54, obtains a type byte offset through 0x82F18250, reads G+0x1D4+t and calls the selected sampler setter. 0x82517698 separately dispatches dirty sampler records.

deviceDispatchReads.label: V
deviceDispatchReads.claim: For 101 entries, the client reads and calls G+0x224+4*i, then stores returned r3 into renderer wrapper+0x12C+8*i. Getter results are replayable state values, not arbitrary success codes.

deviceDispatchReads.label: V
deviceDispatchReads.claim: For thirteen selected types per sampler, the client reads and calls G+0x3B8+t with r4=stage and stores returned r3 into renderer wrapper+0x454+8*j. The type table and outer sampler count remain inputs.

inlineReadModifyWrites.label: V
inlineReadModifyWrites.claim: The client loads its cached device through receiver+0xB8, writes G+0x780..0x7BC and reads/ORs/stores G+0 with bit63. The float shadow overlaps SetVertexShaderConstantF 0x82692588, which this path bypasses.

inlineReadModifyWrites.label: V
inlineReadModifyWrites.claim: The client loads receiver+0xB8, writes G+0x1780..0x178C and reads/ORs/stores G+0x8 with bit63, bypassing SetPixelShaderConstantF 0x82692668.

inlineReadModifyWrites.label: V
inlineReadModifyWrites.claim: After loading G through renderer wrapper+0xF54, the client reads/merges/stores G+0x48C, then reads/ORs/stores G+0x18 with low-word mask0x80000000. The accepted +0xEE0 store belongs to the renderer wrapper, not G.

readbackBoundary.label: I
readbackBoundary.claim: If guest getters survive, replacement setters must maintain the state they read, including retention. Replacing both getter and setter can move that state to a host registry. Title-side table loads and direct writes still require guest storage or explicit caller replacement.

entries.fields: G+0x2E2C declaration; FVF 0x826946D8 is an additional writer

readbackBoundary.qualification: These are library getter reads requested by outside clients, not direct title loads of each binding. Constants also have requested readback in native-renderer-world-constant-dataflow. A retained getter makes its specific header and AddRef dependencies relevant.

publishedDeviceAliases.label: V
publishedDeviceAliases.claim: The first caller requests G into SP+0xBC. 0x8258B038 requests it into incoming object+0x10, so it escapes into retained storage. 0x82662D28 and 0x82662E70 request SP+0x58, compare G with owner+0xC and release it at 0x82662E5C and 0x82662FA4.
publishedDeviceAliases.qualification: These are outside-region clients, including utility code of unclosed ownership. Partial caller windows and unknown engine-object virtual calls do not close all copied aliases.

objectAndBlobClients.label: V
objectAndBlobClients.shaderPointerCaches: 0x824FF578 calls CreateVertexShader at0x824FF640 and stores the result to owner+0x73C at0x824FF648. 0x824FF690 calls CreatePixelShader at0x824FF758 and stores owner+0x740 at0x824FF760. Both obtain the compiled input through an indirect compiler vtable+0xC call. Their local bodies do not store a separate compiled-blob field.
objectAndBlobClients.thinCreationClients: 0x825584C8 and0x82558518 forward incoming r4 as the compiled input at0x825584D8 and0x82558528, test for null and return the created pointer or error-path zero. These bounded bodies do not retain the input descriptor.
objectAndBlobClients.compilationLifetime: 0x82302208 and0x82302348 pass compiler output to creation at0x823022E0 and0x82302474, retain returned shader pointers and invoke temporary compiler-object Release through vtable+8. The compiler object's other aliases and actual release semantics remain unbound.
objectAndBlobClients.externalHeaderConstruction: 0x82534428,0x82534508 and0x82534AA0 allocate or pool a32-byte VB header, independently of CreateVertexBuffer0x826982A8. Fresh-header construction invokes0x826B6C40 and installs backing through0x826B71A8. The pooled-return arm of0x82534508 instead loads the selected header into r30 from the pool and directly stores1 to header+4 at0x825345FC before returning it. Hooking only resource allocation APIs would miss this refcount reinitialization.
objectAndBlobClients.qualification: Fresh native windows confirmed selected call, null-test and cache-store words. No outside direct microcode, variant or declaration-element access was identified in the sampled client windows, but other aliases, IB/texture/surface prefixes and optional creation callbacks at*0x82F9B084/*0x82F9B088 remain unclosed. The ordinary creation path's metadata/code copies do not prove all callers relinquish the blob.

outsideReturnUses.label: V
outsideReturnUses.refcounts: 0x82302538 has no explicit local test/store of its sampled Release results. The final0x82302600 Release result can remain in r3 through the wrapper return; ultimate caller use and the wrapper return ABI remain unclosed. 0x82304C68 discards its sampled Release/AddRef counts and later supplies its own success/failure value. Side effects and other count consumers remain relevant.
outsideReturnUses.fenceWrapper: 0x823062D0 calls0x8269C150 at0x823062E4 and forwards r3 through its epilogue. This does not identify the final fence-core result semantics.
outsideReturnUses.busy: 0x8251BD90 calls0x8269C738 at0x8251BDA0 and derives a one-bit return through cntlzw/rlwinm. Outside clients0x8252DD88,0x8252DF88,0x8252E430 and0x82531970 compare the busy result with zero at call postsites0x8252DE4C,0x8252E054,0x8252E4E0 and0x82531ABC. Replacing it with an arbitrary constant changes a surviving control-flow input.
outsideReturnUses.qualification: Exact outside-client windows classify selected return uses. Engine/gameplay ownership, all remaining callsites, busy completion timing and setter residual-r3 use remain unclosed.

searchBounds.publicationSyntax: 20 aligned executable lis0x8200/lwz+0x09F0 candidate pairs within eight words, all inside the surveyed region. Intervening register writes were unchecked. No outside-region match in this exact syntax was found.
searchBounds.splitMaterializer: ghidra/FindSplitConstantCandidates.java: value0x820009F0, lookahead8, cap128; zero candidates, not truncated.
searchBounds.alignedLiteral: ghidra/FindPointerValues.java: value0x820009F0, full-word mask, cap1000; zero matches.
searchBounds.qualification: None covers long-distance address materialization, arbitrary copied bases, indexed accesses, bulk copies or indirect dispatch. This does not establish every G or object reader/writer.

patcherDirectCalls.label: V
patcherDirectCalls.query: ghidra/FindDirectCallers.java: initialized executable aligned raw branch-and-link words; cap256 per entry, no truncation or cancellation.
patcherDirectCalls.claim: Every matched call site belongs to the accepted D3D draw/patch consumer graph. No outside-client direct linked call was found by this query.
patcherDirectCalls.qualification: Tail branches with LK=0, indirect calls, pointer aliases and runtime activation were not closed. No title-wide absence of microcode or declaration access follows.

referenceExample.borrowedFact: The pinned example combined API replacements with guest state: readback shadows, writable upload/lock storage and resource lifetime behavior; selected constant and render-state paths still called the guest bodies. Its ring stubs were part of that project's larger replacement boundary.
referenceExample.qualification: Methodology example only. Its addresses, layouts, ABI assumptions, coverage and stub safety do not transfer to this image.

candidateContract.label: I

hookFamilies.role: coherent device creation/reset and published guest identity
resource creation, writable lock backing, descriptor and parent semantics
bindings, viewport, readback and lifetime changes; preserve or replace matching getters
scratch-producing/commit pair and draw issue paths; BeginVertices/EndVertices names remain candidate aliases
pass, resolve, clear and presentation operations

candidateContract.conditionalEntries: Scissor writer0x8268F9C0 and alternate tiling pair0x8269D7D8/0x8269DB20 retain candidate API identities. Known middleware and XGraphics resource/header paths require classification and inclusion when they survive. The core hook list is not an exhaustive cut set.
candidateContract.guestStorage: Preserve valid G and four dispatch tables while title table clients remain. Preserve writable constant/fetch shadows and visible readback, pointer identity/null/failure conventions, object retention and writable returned upload/lock storage. Preserve or explicitly bridge the pooled VB header+4 reset when that client survives. An opaque host handle alone is not yet a proved replacement for a guest object.
initialGuestBodies: Keep table initialization0x826A5C50 or reproduce its exact selected dispatch/default state before title loads those slots.

Keep shader constant setters0x82692588/0x82692668/0x82692788/0x826927E8/0x82692848/0x826928A0 and render/sampler setter/getter bodies initially; bridge host state from the same shadows. Replace their bodies only with matching ABI, state and return behavior.
Keep known inline title writers; observe their shadow changes before host draws. Function-body setter hooks alone cannot see them.

Keep selected readback and resource/device AddRef/Release behavior until an equivalent identity, refcount, parent, deferred-release and completion model replaces it. Guest header readers still constrain that model.

Keep or replace externally consumed waits/callbacks coherently with their producers. Do not stub ring waits while leaving a caller that needs a returned scratch pointer, completion transition or event.
candidateContract.eliminatedInterior: If all consumers are inside the replaced subgraph, the host does not have to reproduce AD150-patched bytes, variant caches, replay command storage or internal cursor values merely because a D3D body used them. No unique original guest body is intrinsically mandatory after its complete observable contract has been replaced. This is the reason to investigate the API boundary; the cut and aliases remain unproved.

unresolved.nextStatic: Bind the type, consumers and destructor of the object whose+0x10 receives G at0x8258B1C8; close the uninspected remainder of0x82578658 and renderer-wrapper/global copied bases in separate packets of at most eight exact functions.
unresolved.runtimeDiscriminator: Separately authorized read-only access observations on the retained G allocation across create/reset/get/set/draw/present; identify every access whose executing PC is outside the accepted replaced-function set.

unresolved.nextStatic: Follow known external creator/header-builder clients and retained getter outputs; classify each load/store by proven object base rather than displacement alone. Stop at an unknown required writer or dispatch.
unresolved.runtimeDiscriminator: Observe created object extents and code/blob extents for outside-set reads/writes from creation to final release, including middleware and reset.

unresolved.nextStatic: Join the four dispatch-table clients and all nine accepted inline writers to the chosen host state reader, including requested constant readback.
unresolved.runtimeDiscriminator: Compare the state consumed by a host draw after a table-setter change and after each inline shadow change, without using a setter hook as the sole observer.

unresolved.nextStatic: Bind actual optional creation callbacks, setter return consumers and external fence/event waiters; preserve constructor-specific surface parent semantics.
unresolved.runtimeDiscriminator: Record pointer/null/HRESULT paths, AddRef/Release transitions and returns, callback arguments/order, resource fence completion, waited event identity and scratch pointer use before selecting stubs.

guards: Do not claim exhaustive reader/writer closure from the bounded global-cell or displacement scans.
Do not classify a function as D3D solely from its address or an outside function as gameplay solely from being outside the surveyed region.
Do not transfer ReBlue addresses, offsets, ABI assumptions, stub safety or object layouts to this image.
Do not require every D3D-internal field when its consumers are replaced together, or discard a surviving guest dependency merely because the host tracks an equivalent value.
No runtime execution, renderer implementation, title/SDK edits, project repair, save or cutover was established by this finding.
conclusion: An API-level replacement is a plausible candidate, with concrete guest constraints: title table loads and cached getter results, direct constant/fetch read-modify-writes, retained device/object identities, and surviving lifetime/completion interfaces. The bounded direct-call evidence places the selected patcher calls inside the D3D draw graph, but copied object/device aliases and indirect calls prevent an exhaustive cut proof. Research does not establish that opaque objects or ring stubs are safe.
